title: Runtime metric gap list for Standard Cost Model (v1) — missing/ambiguous metrics + instrumentation plan
content:
Context
- This doc tracks runtime-exported metrics required by the Standard Cost Model Spec + API (cost-model v1), and the current gaps/ambiguities blocking accurate per-request cost attribution + drift monitoring.
- Primary consumers: Cost Model service (platform), Telemetry ingestion + aggregation, Console cost breakdowns, Optimize what-if modeling.
- This is intentionally a working doc (expect churn). Canonical field semantics will live in the schema package + Confluence spec; here we focus on “what do we need from runtime” and “how do we instrument it safely”.

Owners
- Runtime scheduling & batching: Sofia Ivanova
- KV cache + prefill/decode accounting: Omar El-Sayed
- Kernel path + quantization identifiers: Grace Kim
- Telemetry pipeline + data quality gates: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
- Aggregation perf / cardinality constraints: Thomas Baird

Guiding principles (v1)
1) Deterministic per-request counters when possible; sampled metrics only when explicitly marked.
2) Bounded cardinality: prefer enums/IDs over freeform strings; avoid per-layer/per-kernel unbounded labels.
3) Split “request-attributable” vs “shared overhead” inputs cleanly (overhead allocation handled by cost-model policy, not runtime).
4) Define precise units + boundaries: tokens vs sub-tokens, ms vs us, bytes vs MiB, inclusive/exclusive intervals.

Quick summary: top gaps blocking cost-model v1
- Prefill vs decode token/time split is inconsistent across runtimes and broken under certain streaming paths (see Slack bug thread).
- KV cache: request-level cache hit/miss accounting is not standardized (esp. partial prefix matches + multi-turn chat) and unit definitions differ.
- Batching efficiency: we lack a stable, request-level “effective batch” / “share of batch compute” signal. Current queue-time is available but not consistently attributed.
- Quantization: missing stable quantization execution path identifier + per-request “profile applied” + fallback reason.
- Speculative/assisted decoding paths: if enabled, we need to know which tokens were produced by which path (or we must disable for v1 cost accuracy claims).

Metric gap list (detailed)
Format:
- Priority: P0 (required for v1 launch), P1 (strongly desired), P2 (nice-to-have / v2)
- Scope: per-request vs per-batch vs per-worker
- Export: runtime -> telemetry (OTel/log) -> cost-model input contract

-------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Prefill/decode token accounting (P0)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need
- request_tokens_prefill: integer tokens
- request_tokens_decode: integer tokens
- request_tokens_total: integer tokens (sanity = prefill + decode)
- request_time_ms_prefill: wall-clock ms spent in prefill stage attributable to request
- request_time_ms_decode: wall-clock ms spent in decode stage attributable to request
- request_time_ms_total: total runtime time (sanity)
- stage_boundary_definition: explicit definition of where prefill ends and decode begins for each model architecture

Current state / gap
- We have “total prompt tokens” and “total output tokens” from metering, but runtime stage split is:
  - Missing in some execution paths (streaming + early stop)
  - Not aligned when prefix cache is used (prefill can be partially skipped; we still need stage counters)
  - Suspect bug with prefill/decode split under continuous batching (see slack:eng-runtime/1769007005)

Proposed instrumentation
- Add explicit per-request stage counters emitted by runtime at completion:
  - tokens_processed_prefill / tokens_processed_decode
  - time_ns_prefill / time_ns_decode
- Include a boolean: used_prefix_cache (true/false) and prefix_cache_tokens_reused (int) (ties into KV cache section)
- Ensure stage time attribution semantics are consistent under continuous batching:
  - time = sum of “request share” of batch step wall-clock (see batching section) OR explicitly define as “time in system within stage” (queue+compute)
  - For v1 cost model we mainly need compute share; if we can’t do share, we must export both “compute_time” and “queue_time” separately.

Owner: Omar El-Sayed
Tracking: linear:ENG-4828 (runtime metrics), linear:ENG-4823 (telemetry input contract)
Risks
- Attribution correctness under batching is the hardest part. If we can’t provide compute share, cost model will approximate using batch-level GPU-time and token shares.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
2) KV cache / prefix cache metrics (P0)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need (request-level)
- kv_cache_hit_rate_request: float 0..1 (definition: fraction of prefill tokens skipped due to cache reuse)
- kv_cache_tokens_reused: int (tokens)
- kv_cache_tokens_computed: int (tokens)
- kv_cache_lookup_latency_ms: float (optional P1)
- kv_cache_evictions_count: int (P1)
- kv_cache_eviction_reason: enum (capacity, ttl, manual, other) (P2)

Ambiguities to resolve
- Partial prefix match:
  - If first N tokens match cache, we count N reused, remainder computed.
- Multi-turn chat:
  - cache reuse may happen across turns; ensure we attribute reuse to the request benefiting from it.
- Quantization interaction:
  - cache formats can differ by quant profile; reuse may be blocked; need a “cache_compatibility_key” or a boolean “cache_reuse_blocked_by_profile”.

Current state / gap
- Cache hit/miss metric names differ across runtime versions; some export per-worker metrics only.
- Token metering sees fewer compute tokens but cannot explain why; Console wants explicit “cache savings” line item.

Proposed instrumentation
- Standardize runtime counters + names as part of the cost-model telemetry contract.
- Emit per-request:
  - kv_cache_tokens_reused
  - kv_cache_tokens_requested (prefill tokens)
  - kv_cache_hit_rate_request = reused / requested
- Emit per-worker periodic gauges (optional): kv_cache_bytes_used, kv_cache_bytes_capacity

Owner: Omar El-Sayed (runtime) + Logan Wright (telemetry contract)
Tracking: github:redwood/pr-28483 (naming contract), github:redwood/pr-28509 (runtime export)

-------------------------------------------------------------------
3) Batch efficiency / compute share (P0)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need
- batch_id: opaque ID (per batch step) (P1; useful for debugging but watch cardinality)
- request_compute_share: float 0..1 (per request, sum across batch steps ~ 1 request “unit” of work)
- batch_size_effective: float (e.g., harmonic mean of batch sizes across steps attributable to request)
- batch_size_max_observed: int (optional)
- queue_time_ms: float (time waiting in scheduler/queue)
- scheduling_delay_ms: float (optional; differentiates queue vs admission control)

Current state / gap
- We have batch_size at the batch level and queue time at worker level, but we cannot reliably attribute “how much GPU time did this request consume” under continuous batching.
- Telemetry currently exports some batch efficiency metrics but they’re not stable enough to put in a cross-product contract (see slack:eng-runtime/1768512097).

Proposed instrumentation (v1 pragmatic)
Option A (preferred): token-based compute share
- For each decode step and prefill step, attribute compute share proportional to tokens for request in that step:
  - share_step = request_tokens_step / total_tokens_in_batch_step
- Aggregate per request:
  - request_compute_share = sum(share_step * step_wall_time_ms)
  - Also export batch_wall_time_ms_total so cost-model can reconcile.

Option B (fallback): effective batch factor only
- Export per request:
  - effective_batch_factor_decode (float)
  - effective_batch_factor_prefill (float)
- Cost-model uses these as multipliers against per-token GPU-time curves.

Owner: Sofia Ivanova (scheduler/runtime), Thomas Baird (cardinality/perf review)
Tracking: github:redwood/pr-28479 (batch efficiency), linear:ENG-4828
Notes
- We must cap label cardinality: avoid exporting per-batch IDs to all telemetry streams by default. Consider debug-only sampling keyed by request_id hash.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
4) Quantization profile + execution path identifiers (P0)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need
- quant_profile_id: stable ID (string from model catalog; not freeform)
- quant_method: enum (fp16, bf16, int8, int4, awq, gptq, marlin, other) [final list TBD]
- quant_fallback: boolean
- quant_fallback_reason: enum (unsupported_op, accuracy_guardrail, hardware_mismatch, kernel_missing, other)
- kernel_path_id: stable ID for the selected kernel/engine path (bounded enum or hashed mapping maintained in runtime)

Current state / gap
- Optimize needs to model quant ROI; cost-model needs to know what path actually ran.
- Today we often know the intended profile (config) but not the executed path (fallbacks happen silently).

Proposed instrumentation
- Runtime emits per request:
  - quant_profile_id (from model catalog)
  - executed_precision (enum) and kernel_path_id
  - fallback boolean + reason
- Model catalog must expose stable quant_profile_id + metadata (coord with platform team).

Owner: Grace Kim
Tracking: linear:ENG-4829 (catalog IDs), cost-model schema v1 alignment

-------------------------------------------------------------------
5) GPU time attribution inputs (P1)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need
- gpu_time_ms_request_estimate OR gpu_time_ms_batch_total (and a share function)
- sm_utilization_avg (per worker, sampled) (optional)
- mem_bw_utilization_avg (per worker, sampled) (optional)

Current state / gap
- We can estimate cost from token counts + known curves, but drift monitoring benefits from an independent “GPU-time-ish” signal.

Proposed instrumentation
- Export per-batch “gpu_step_time_ms” and per-request share (see batching section).
- Avoid per-kernel metrics in v1.

Owner: Sofia Ivanova + Grace Kim

-------------------------------------------------------------------
6) Memory pressure + KV cache capacity signals (P1)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need
- kv_cache_bytes_used (gauge)
- kv_cache_bytes_capacity (gauge)
- kv_cache_pressure_ratio (derived)
- oom_events_count (counter)
- kv_cache_compaction_events (optional)

Why
- Explains why cache hit rate may drop and why latencies spike; helps Optimize recommendations avoid destabilizing changes.

Owner: Omar El-Sayed

-------------------------------------------------------------------
7) Routing / model version / replica context needed by runtime (P0, but may already exist upstream)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need from runtime telemetry (only if not guaranteed by control plane logs)
- model_id, model_version
- engine_version (runtime build/version)
- hardware_sku (A10, L4, A100, H100, etc.)
- region / cluster

Notes
- Some of these are better sourced from infra metadata, but cost-model input contract requires them to be present/derivable.

Owner: Ethan Park (API) + Logan Wright (telemetry)

-------------------------------------------------------------------
8) Speculative decoding / assisted generation flags (P2 for v1; P1 if enabled in prod)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need
- decoding_strategy: enum (standard, speculative, assisted, other)
- draft_model_id (if speculative)
- accepted_tokens_count vs proposed_tokens_count

Current state
- Not universally enabled. If enabled, cost needs to reflect extra compute.

Owner: Grace Kim

-------------------------------------------------------------------
9) Cache “warm rate” / cacheability signal for what-if modeling (P2)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What we need
- cache_warm_rate_estimate: float 0..1 at workload level (NOT per-request)

Notes
- This is likely not a runtime metric; better derived in Optimize from request traces/prompt similarity.
- Mentioned here because Optimize asked for it; we should keep it out of the runtime contract for now.

Owner: Hassan Mirza (Optimize) + Logan Wright (telemetry)

Cardinality + performance constraints (must-follow)
- No unbounded string labels emitted per request (prompt hash, user ID, tool name, etc.).
- Enumerate kernel_path_id and quant_fallback_reason; if new values needed, gate via runtime release.
- Per-batch IDs only in debug mode and sampled (e.g., 0.1%) with a fixed allowlist of tenants/environments.

Data quality checks (telemetry)
- Hard invariants (drop/flag events when violated):
  - tokens_total == tokens_prefill + tokens_decode
  - 0 <= kv_cache_hit_rate_request <= 1
  - kv_cache_tokens_reused <= request_tokens_prefill
  - quant_fallback_reason present iff quant_fallback == true
- Soft invariants (alert only):
  - sudden shifts in stage split distribution per model version
  - cache hit rate > 0 with cache bytes used near 0 (likely instrumentation bug)

Open questions
1) Do we define request_time_ms_prefill/decode as compute-only, or as time-in-system for that stage?
   - Cost model wants compute. Console wants latency too, but it can use separate latency metrics.
   - Proposal: export both compute_time_ms_* and queue_time_ms (and optionally end_to_end_ms).
2) Under continuous batching, can we implement a stable compute share without heavy overhead?
   - Option: compute share via token ratios + batch step wall time.
   - Validate overhead with perf budget; gate behind feature flag initially.
3) How do we represent “prefix cache” vs “KV cache” naming?
   - Proposal: treat prefix cache as “kv_cache” in taxonomy; clarify in schema docs.

Next steps (2-week plan)
- (Runtime) Omar: patch + validate prefill/decode split bug; add per-request counters behind feature flag. Target: end of week 1.
- (Runtime) Sofia: propose batching attribution method (Option A vs B) + perf estimate. Target: mid-week 1.
- (Runtime) Grace: draft bounded enums for quant_method, kernel_path_id, fallback reasons. Target: end of week 1.
- (Telemetry) Logan/Nadia: update telemetry input contract + validators; define dashboards for invariants. Target: week 2.
- (Review) Thomas: cardinality/perf review; sign-off on any per-batch identifiers/sampling plan. Target: week 2.

Appendix: proposed canonical metric names (draft)
- rw.runtime.tokens.prefill
- rw.runtime.tokens.decode
- rw.runtime.time_ms.prefill_compute
- rw.runtime.time_ms.decode_compute
- rw.runtime.queue_time_ms
- rw.runtime.kv_cache.tokens_reused
- rw.runtime.kv_cache.tokens_requested
- rw.runtime.kv_cache.hit_rate
- rw.runtime.quant.profile_id
- rw.runtime.quant.method
- rw.runtime.quant.executed_precision
- rw.runtime.quant.fallback
- rw.runtime.quant.fallback_reason
- rw.runtime.kernel.path_id

Notes to self (Omar)
- Keep a tight loop with cost-model schema owners: don’t ship metric names that don’t map 1:1 to schema fields.
- When in doubt, export raw counters (tokens/time) rather than derived ratios; derive ratios in cost-model so we can fix logic without redeploying runtime.
